//: Story Phase 5, chapter 21: What Do You Actually Do? Late morning. A shark takes a bite out of the port rail and everyone runs to Shark Duty except the Grand Stenchmaster. The crew confront him at his chair (14,18), facing the sheet over the thing at (14,17): seat readiness, Frog Grog quality assurance, strategic releases, executive readiness and, finally, television. The Stenchmaster Entertainment System is unveiled; the captain looks at it himself (the S.E.S. close-up); then the qualifications argument, the captain's definition, a CRAAACK, and 'Back to work.'
p5c2.begin: The whole deck jumps. Splinters spin up past the port rail. Somewhere below, a board that was Gerald is now two boards.
Twenty pirates grab twenty poles, mops and oars and run for the port rail.
Nineteen pirates. One of them stays exactly where he is, in his chair, in front of the sheet.

p5c2.begin.tutorial: Shark Duty! See off the sharks at the port rail. (Walk to the red marker, face the rail, press Confirm and strike on the green.)
p5c2.begin.title: What Do You Actually Do?

p5c2.ask_hint: garrick[businesslike]: Can't talk, Captain. On duty.
p5c2.watch_done: The last of the sharks sinks back with a sulky swirl. The crew lean on their poles, gasping.
Every one of them, as one, turns to look at the chair.
pete[annoyed]: Four hours. Four hours we've been beating sharks off this boat since sunrise.

p5c2.watch_done.tutorial: Ask the Grand Stenchmaster what, exactly, he's been doing. (His chair, midships, by the Forecast Board.)
p5c2.watch_done.title: What Do You Actually Do?

p5c2.confront: garrick[smug]: Captain! And... everyone. How lovely. Is it a ceremony?
captain[determined]: Garrick. The ship is being eaten.
garrick[businesslike]: I'm aware. I can hear it from here. It's very distracting.
gristle[annoyed]: Then why are ye SITTING there?
garrick[proud]: Because, Mister Gristle, I am at my post. Performing the duties of my office.
There is a pause in which nineteen people think the same thing at the same time. Bob is the one who says it.
bob[surprised]: What duties?

p5c2.confront.say: crew: WHAT EXACTLY DOES A GRAND STENCHMASTER DO?
p5c2.confront.name: Everyone

p5c2.confront: garrick[delighted]: I'm SO glad you asked.
He produces a galley tray from under his chair. Pinned to it is a sheet of paper, crayoned in six colours.

p5c2.confront.caption: His own list, in crayon, on a galley tray.

p5c2.confront: garrick[businesslike]: First and foremost: seat readiness.
gristle[surprised]: Seat readiness?
garrick[businesslike]: A cold chair reflects poorly on management.
pete[alarmed]: THE SHIP IS BEING EATEN BY SHARKS!
garrick[smug]: And yet you'll notice my chair is perfectly prepared.
bob: Prepared for what?
garrick[businesslike]: Sitting.

p5c2.confront.say: crew: SITTING?! / HE'S BEEN SITTING! / I'll prepare HIS chair! / Somebody hold me back!
p5c2.confront.name: The crew

p5c2.confront: garrick[businesslike]: Allow me to demonstrate.
He stands up.
He sits back down, very slowly, with enormous care, the way a hen settles on an egg.
garrick[proud]: You see? Warm. Ready. Prepared for any eventuality.
captain: Get up and help.
garrick[businesslike]: That would let the seat go cold, Captain. Then where would we be?
He does not get up. He wriggles slightly, to show how not-getting-up he is.
garrick[businesslike]: Second duty: Frog Grog. Quality assurance.
jim[angry]: Ye DRINK it! Ye just sit there and DRINK it while everybody else works!
garrick[businesslike]: Quality assurance.
jim[angry]: It tastes WORSE every DAY!
garrick[proud]: Exactly. Which is why continuous testing is necessary.
garrick[proud]: Third duty, and the chief one. The CEREMONIAL duty. Strategic releases.
rook[disgusted]: He means farting.
garrick[offended]: I mean pressure management. Atmospheric release. Scent maintenance. Shark diversion, in emergencies. It's a very technical field.
gristle[annoyed]: Yer 'strategic release' is WHY the sharks are eating the SHIP!
pete[annoyed]: The first one blew up the treasure room!
bob: And the beard!
squawks[insulting]: And the bird.
garrick[businesslike]: Gentlemen. We are discussing present responsibilities. Not legacy liabilities.
garrick[businesslike]: Fourth duty. Rest. Or, as it's properly called: executive readiness.
pete[annoyed]: You've been ASLEEP half the morning!
garrick[smug]: Readiness.
gristle[annoyed]: You were SNORING!
garrick[smug]: Deep readiness.
bob[disgusted]: You drooled on the Stench Log.
garrick[businesslike]: Administrative moisture.
The noise the crew make at this point is not words. It is the sound a kettle makes, just before it stops being a kettle.
captain[angry]: And what have ye been DOING? All morning? Facing a SHEET?
garrick[proud]: Ah. That would be my fifth duty.
He rises from his chair, at last, with the air of a man about to unveil a statue of himself.
garrick[proud]: Gentlemen. Captain. I have been monitoring...
garrick[delighted]: ...THE STENCHMASTER ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM.
He whips the sailcloth away.
It is a box. Probably. It is mostly a box.

It is a crate with a great, round, bulging pane of thick green glass set into the front of it, like a ship's porthole that has swallowed something. Two enormous brass knobs. Glass tubes along the top, glowing orange. A frying pan on a stick. A broken compass, for some reason, set into the side. A coil of copper. Two forks, bent into an aerial. And everywhere, out of every crack, wires.
The glass is full of hissing grey snow.
gristle[disgusted]: That is not a television.
garrick[smug]: Certainly is.
pete[alarmed]: It has a FUSE.
garrick[businesslike]: Picture stabilisation.
jim[alarmed]: There is a CANNON PRIMER wired to the back!
garrick[businesslike]: Signal amplification.
bob: Why is there a potato nailed to it?
garrick[businesslike]: Grounding.
bob: That's not how grounding works.
garrick[smug]: Are YOU a Grand Stenchmaster, Mister Bob?
bob: ...No.
garrick[proud]: Then we have established jurisdiction.
captain: It looks like a bomb.
rook: It looks like a bomb that's been to a jumble sale.
garrick[offended]: It is a precision instrument.
captain: What is it MADE of?

garrick[businesslike]: Oh, this and that. A broken lantern. Some spare wire. The compass from the jolly boat. Some cutlery, a cannon lock, a few bottles. A bit of the old bell, from when it cracked. The barometer off the forecast equipment. Odds and ends I found.
jory[annoyed]: 'Found'.
garrick[smug]: They were lying about.
jory[annoyed]: They were BOLTED DOWN.
pete: None of those things can become a television.
quill[surprised]: I've a list of everything in it. None of it is a television. Not one piece. Not even TOGETHER.
garrick[proud]: And yet.
He reaches past you and turns the big brass knob, one click.
The snow parts. On the thick green glass, in grainy grey, a little stage appears, with a curtain. A man in a ruff stands on it, shaking his finger at a turnip.
The turnip does not reply. The man seems to take this badly.
Nineteen pirates stare at the screen, and then at each other, and then at the screen.
There is no aerial anywhere for a thousand miles. There are no theatres for a thousand miles. There are definitely no turnips.
It is not possible. It is very plainly happening.
garrick[smug]: The screen works.

p5c2.confront.tutorial: Have a look at the Stenchmaster Entertainment System yourself. (Stand beside it and press Confirm.)
p5c2.confront.title: What Do You Actually Do?

p5c2.ses_first: You step up to the Stenchmaster Entertainment System. It hums at you. The glass is warm, like a forehead.
p5c2.reactions: You straighten up. The crew are still there. All of them. Waiting, the way a crowd waits for a hanging.
pete[annoyed]: We have been beating sharks away for FOUR HOURS!
garrick[businesslike]: And I've been monitoring channel integrity.
gristle[annoyed]: You were watching a man argue with a TURNIP!
garrick[offended]: Important cultural programming.
jim[angry]: A shark ate half me food locker!
garrick[annoyed]: I know. I missed the ending because of all the shouting.
jim[angry]: GOOD!
bob: Does it help with the sharks?
garrick[businesslike]: Not currently.
bob: The Center?
garrick: No.
bob: Repairs?
garrick: No.
bob: Then what does it DO?
garrick[proud]: Entertainment.
Somewhere in the long silence that follows, a shark bumps the hull. Nobody looks round.

p5c2.reactions.say: crew: ENTERTAINMENT?! / FOR WHO?! / FOR HIM! / I'LL ENTERTAIN HIM!
p5c2.reactions.name: The crew

p5c2.reactions: gristle[annoyed]: WHY are you even the Grand Stenchmaster?!
garrick[businesslike]: Because nobody else aboard is qualified.
gristle[annoyed]: QUALIFIED? YE INVENTED THE JOB!
garrick[smug]: Entrepreneurship.
pete[annoyed]: What qualification does it even REQUIRE?
garrick[businesslike]: Experience.
pete[alarmed]: EXPERIENCE DOING WHAT?
Garrick gestures, grandly, round the whole ship: the stains, the patches, the yellow haze, the fins, the bald parrot.
jim[angry]: I cook for forty men every day while a poisonous cloud wanders through me KITCHEN!
garrick[businesslike]: Different department.
bob[disgusted]: I've been patching shark holes since SUNRISE!
garrick[happy]: Excellent initiative.
bob[alarmed]: I AM NOT APPLYING FOR YOUR APPROVAL!
ned[alarmed]: I can see five hundred sharks from the masthead!
garrick[businesslike]: Which is why you are the lookout, Mister Ned, and I am the Stenchmaster.
gristle[annoyed]: The stench is YOURS!
garrick[proud]: Precisely why I'm uniquely qualified.
pete[annoyed]: So if I set fire to the galley, does that make me Grand FIREmaster?
Garrick actually thinks about it. You can see him do it.
garrick[businesslike]: ...Depends how impressive the fire is.
jim[angry]: DON'T YOU DARE GIVE HIM IDEAS ABOUT MY GALLEY!
captain[determined]: ENOUGH.
It is the voice that used to make admirals spill their tea. The deck goes quiet.
captain[determined]: Garrick. One sentence. A USEFUL definition. What does a Grand Stenchmaster do?
garrick[businesslike]: Certainly, Captain.
He clears his throat.

garrick[proud]: The Grand Stenchmaster maintains seat temperature, monitors broadcasts, evaluates the Frog Grog, conducts scent inspections, issues forecasts, preserves digestive readiness, performs strategic releases, attends to ceremonial matters, and rests between responsibilities.
You stare at him for a long time.
captain[tired]: ...Ye have invented a royal office for being lazy.
garrick[delighted]: At LAST. Someone who understands.
captain[angry]: THAT WAS NOT PRAISE.
CRAAAAACK.

p5c2.reactions.text: SHARK DUTY! PORT RAIL! THEY'RE BACK!

p5c2.reactions: The crew scatter for their poles, swearing.
Garrick dusts off his knees, sits back down in his chair, and reaches for the big brass knob.
You turn around. Very, very slowly.
captain: Where are ye going?
garrick[businesslike]: Back to work.
captain[angry]: THAT IS NOT WORK.
garrick[smug]: Contractual disagreement.
